examples.normal: Did you have time for any sightseeing during your trip?
examples.hard: We spent the morning sightseeing in the old city and the afternoon relaxing by the hotel pool.

examples.normal: The trek to the mountain village took us six hours.
examples.hard: After a three-day trek through the mountains, we were tired but happy to see the lake at last.

examples.normal: Madrid is the capital of Spain.
examples.hard: The capital has grown so quickly that many people now live in new districts far from the centre.

examples.normal: Don't let one bad day ruin your whole holiday.
examples.hard: The scandal ruined his career, and he never worked in politics again.

examples.easy: This jacket is just my size.
examples.normal: That's just what I needed after a long day.
examples.hard: The hotel was just as beautiful as the photos, and the staff were incredibly friendly.

examples.easy: He gave me a new banknote.
examples.normal: The cashier checked the banknote to make sure it was real.
examples.hard: The police found thousands of banknotes hidden inside an old suitcase in the basement.

examples.normal: The medicine made me feel groggy all afternoon.
examples.hard: After the long night flight, she felt groggy and couldn't concentrate during the morning meeting.

examples.normal: The cashier gave me the wrong change by mistake.
examples.hard: The supermarket has replaced some cashiers with self-service machines, but many customers still prefer a person.

examples.normal: He took his credit card out of his wallet and paid.
examples.hard: Someone found my wallet on the bus and handed it in, with all the cards and money still inside.

examples.normal: Listening to podcasts can really help your pronunciation.
examples.hard: Some English words have two possible pronunciations, depending on whether the speaker is British or American.

examples.easy: Take your anorak, it might rain.
examples.normal: He put on his anorak and went out into the wind.
examples.hard: My mum always made me take my anorak to school, even when the sky was perfectly clear.

examples.normal: My daughter coloured the picture with red and yellow crayons.
examples.hard: The restaurant gives every child a box of crayons and a paper menu to draw on while they wait.

examples.easy: I had a nightmare last night.
examples.normal: The child woke up crying after a terrible nightmare.
examples.hard: Ever since the accident, he has had nightmares about driving on icy roads at night.

examples.easy: She didn't respond to my email.
examples.normal: Please respond to the invitation by Friday.
examples.hard: The company responded quickly to the complaints and offered every customer a full refund.

examples.normal: I wrote to her last week, but she hasn't replied yet.
examples.hard: When the journalist asked about his plans, the minister replied that he had nothing to add.

examples.normal: In my opinion, the film was too long.
examples.hard: Everyone in the meeting had a different opinion, so it took hours to reach a decision.

examples.normal: Try to avoid foods that contain a lot of fat.
examples.hard: The box contained old letters and photographs that nobody in the family had seen for years.

examples.easy: The statue in the hall is only a replica.
examples.normal: The museum sells small replicas of famous statues.
examples.hard: The ship in the harbour is an exact replica of the one that sailed around the world four centuries ago.

examples.normal: I always forget my colleagues' birthdays, so I set reminders now.
examples.hard: She had completely forgotten about the meeting until her manager called to ask where she was.

examples.normal: Many western countries celebrate Christmas at the end of December.
examples.hard: Western films were extremely popular in the 1960s, especially the ones set in the American desert.

examples.easy: Measure the length of the table.
examples.normal: The length of the bridge is almost two kilometres.
examples.hard: Before buying curtains, we checked the length of the windows twice to make sure they would fit.

examples.normal: He watched in horror as the car slid towards the river.
examples.hard: To our horror, we discovered that the hotel had cancelled our booking and had no free rooms left.

examples.easy: Read the definition in the dictionary.
examples.normal: Can you give me a clear definition of this word, please?
examples.hard: The teacher asked us to write our own definition of success before we looked it up online.

examples.easy: The job involves a lot of travel.
examples.normal: Learning a language involves practising a little every single day.
examples.hard: The new project will involve working closely with engineers from three different departments.

examples.easy: We went on vacation in July.
examples.normal: They spent their summer vacation at a lake in the mountains.
examples.hard: After months of hard work, she finally took a two-week vacation and switched off her phone completely.

examples.normal: She tanned on the beach every afternoon during the holiday.
examples.hard: People with fair skin rarely tan; they usually burn unless they use strong sun cream.

examples.normal: She returned to Tashkent after five years of working abroad.
examples.hard: When we returned from our trip, we found that someone had broken into the garage.

examples.easy: I read an interesting article today.
examples.normal: She writes a weekly article about health for a local newspaper.
examples.hard: The article he published last month caused a heated debate among teachers and parents across the country.

examples.easy: She has the ability to sing.
examples.normal: His ability to stay calm under pressure makes him a great manager.
examples.hard: Employers increasingly value the ability to communicate clearly, both in person and in writing.

examples.normal: The school has special classes for autistic children and their parents.
examples.hard: Many autistic adults find bright lights and loud noises very stressful, so quiet workplaces can help them.

examples.easy: My grandfather is a little deaf.
examples.normal: She learnt sign language to talk with her deaf neighbour.
examples.hard: Although he was born deaf, he became a successful designer and now runs his own company.

examples.normal: Does the ticket include a visit to the museum as well?
examples.hard: The tour package includes flights, hotel accommodation and a guided trip around the old city.

examples.easy: I love learning about Japanese culture.
examples.normal: Food is an important part of the culture in every country.
examples.hard: Living abroad taught her to respect cultures that were very different from her own.

examples.normal: Keep the matches in a dry place, away from the children.
examples.hard: The power went off during the storm, so we lit the candles with the last box of matches we had.

examples.normal: Be careful, the snow is falling off the roof onto the path.
examples.hard: Several rocks fell onto the road after the heavy rain, so the police closed it for the whole day.

examples.normal: The old sofa looked comfortable but very worn and faded.
examples.hard: She still wears her father's worn leather jacket because it reminds her of him.

examples.normal: My daughter practises the violin for an hour every evening.
examples.hard: He started playing the violin at six and was performing with a professional orchestra by the age of twenty.

examples.normal: Good sleep is vital if you want to stay healthy.
examples.hard: It is vital that all passengers read the safety instructions before the plane takes off.

examples.normal: We spent the entire weekend cleaning the house.
examples.hard: The entire team worked late every night to finish the project before the deadline.

examples.normal: I've been to London a couple of times for work.
examples.hard: A couple of tourists stopped me in the street to ask for directions to the old mosque.

examples.normal: The blind man crossed the road with the help of his dog.
examples.hard: Modern phones have special features that help blind people read messages and use the internet.

examples.normal: She works for an international company with offices in ten countries.
examples.hard: The international conference brought together scientists from more than fifty countries to discuss climate change.

examples.normal: Competition between mobile phone companies keeps prices low.
examples.hard: Because of the fierce competition for jobs, graduates need good English and real work experience.

examples.normal: The new flat is nearer to my office than the old one.
examples.hard: As the wedding day got nearer, the bride became more and more nervous about her speech.

examples.normal: She spent her childhood in a small village near Bukhara.
examples.hard: Many of his childhood memories are connected with the long summers he spent at his grandparents' house.

examples.easy: My brother plays in a band.
examples.normal: The band played all their old songs at the concert last night.
examples.hard: After ten years together, the band decided to split up and each member started a solo career.

units.name: Lesson 35 - Present perfect and everyday words

examples.normal: She has already finished her report, so she can go home.
examples.hard: By the time we arrived at the cinema, the film had already started and the hall was dark.

examples.normal: I haven't replied to her email yet, but I will tonight.
examples.hard: The results of the exam haven't been published yet, so the students are still waiting nervously.

examples.normal: Are you still working at the same bank as last year?
examples.hard: Even after twenty years in London, he still speaks English with a strong accent.

examples.normal: My son is good at addition but finds division difficult.
examples.hard: Before calculators became common, shop assistants had to do addition quickly in their heads.

examples.normal: We use the past participle to form the present perfect tense.
examples.hard: Irregular verbs are tricky because their past participles often look completely different from the base form.

examples.normal: He couldn't move his leg after the accident.
examples.hard: The cat sat on the windowsill and watched the birds without moving a single muscle.

examples.normal: The students were confused by the new grammar rule.
examples.hard: If you are confused about the instructions, ask your manager before you start the task.

examples.normal: Do you recall where we parked the car this morning?
examples.hard: She could not recall exactly what the man looked like, but she remembered his red coat.

examples.normal: The majority of students in our class come from Tashkent.
examples.hard: Although the majority voted for the new plan, a few members were strongly against it.

examples.easy: Is there a particular book you want?
examples.normal: She doesn't like any particular type of music; she listens to everything.
examples.hard: On this particular occasion, the manager decided to allow everyone to leave work an hour early.

examples.normal: First, read the questions, and then listen to the recording.
examples.hard: Let me finish this email first, and then we can sit down and talk about your proposal.

examples.normal: He told us a real story about his life in the army.
examples.hard: It was hard to believe the news was real until we saw the pictures on television.

examples.normal: A plumber came to fix the broken pipe in the kitchen.
examples.hard: The water pipes burst during the coldest week of winter, and the whole building was flooded.

examples.normal: All students are encouraged to participate in class discussions.
examples.hard: More than two hundred companies participated in the international trade fair held in Tashkent last year.

examples.normal: The poet was interred in the cemetery of his home town.
examples.hard: According to his wishes, the old general was interred next to his wife in a small village churchyard.

examples.normal: She took some coins out of her purse to pay for the bus.
examples.hard: Someone stole her purse on the crowded metro, so she had to cancel all her bank cards.

examples.normal: Our teacher gave us a difficult writing assignment for Monday.
examples.hard: Students who hand in their assignments late will lose ten per cent of their marks for each extra day.

examples.normal: Tall stone columns stand at the entrance of the theatre.
examples.hard: The roof of the ancient palace was supported by twenty marble columns decorated with flowers.

examples.normal: She found it hard to cope with work and two small children.
examples.hard: After losing his job, he coped with the stress by running every morning and talking to friends.

examples.normal: The children skated on the frozen lake all afternoon.
examples.hard: She had never skated before, but by the end of the holiday she could move confidently on the ice.

examples.normal: They travelled around Europe by train last summer.
examples.hard: Since he started working from home, he has been able to travel more and visit his relatives abroad.

examples.easy: Report the problem to your manager.
examples.normal: The accident was reported on the evening news.
examples.hard: Witnesses reported seeing a man in a black jacket running away from the shop just after midnight.

examples.normal: She works as an engineer for a large construction company.
examples.hard: The engineers who designed the new bridge had to make sure it could survive strong earthquakes.

examples.normal: My aunt was taken to hospital after she fell down the stairs.
examples.hard: The new hospital has modern equipment, but it still doesn't have enough nurses to treat everyone quickly.

examples.normal: My son drew a picture of our family on the kitchen wall.
examples.hard: He could draw a detailed map of the city from memory after living there for only a month.

examples.normal: Her writing style is clear, simple and easy to follow.
examples.hard: The restaurant serves traditional dishes, but they are cooked in a modern style with fresh ingredients.

examples.normal: The sunset over the mountains was absolutely beautiful.
examples.hard: We walked along the beach until sunset and then had dinner at a small fish restaurant nearby.

examples.normal: She keeps meticulous notes on every meeting she attends.
examples.hard: The meticulous planning of the event meant that nothing went wrong, even when two hundred guests arrived at once.

examples.normal: He practises the piano for two hours after work.
examples.hard: If you want to pass the speaking exam, you need to practise talking about familiar topics with a partner.

examples.easy: Learn a new phrase every day.
examples.normal: This phrase is very common in everyday English conversation.
examples.hard: The guidebook includes useful phrases for ordering food, asking for directions and booking a hotel room.

examples.easy: I like the design of this car.
examples.normal: The design of the new website is simple and modern.
examples.hard: The architects presented three different designs for the library, and the city council chose the cheapest one.

units.name: Lesson 37 - Rules, obligations and everyday life

examples.normal: All visitors must report to reception when they arrive.
examples.hard: You must renew your passport before it expires, or you won't be allowed to travel abroad.

examples.normal: Schools are required by law to publish their exam results.
examples.hard: The new law, which comes into force next year, will make it illegal to smoke in parks.

examples.normal: What do you think is the secret of your success?
examples.hard: Her success in business came only after years of failure and many sleepless nights.

examples.normal: We are very obliged to our neighbours for their help.
examples.hard: I would be obliged if you could send me the documents by Friday, as the deadline is close.

examples.normal: Sorry to disturb you, but there is a phone call for you.
examples.hard: He hung a sign on the door so that nobody would disturb him while he was studying.

examples.easy: The keys are inside my bag.
examples.normal: There was a gold watch inside the box on the table.
examples.hard: It started raining heavily, so we stayed inside the museum until the storm had passed.

examples.normal: This antique table belonged to my great-grandmother.
examples.hard: The shop sells antiques from all over Central Asia, including carpets that are over a hundred years old.

examples.easy: There was a rush of air.
examples.normal: The door blew open, letting in a rush of cold air.
examples.hard: When the shop opened its doors, there was a sudden rush of customers looking for bargains.

examples.normal: A penalty in the last minute levelled the score at 2-2.
examples.hard: Although the final score was only 1-0, the home team had controlled the game from the very beginning.

examples.normal: We must get someone to fix that wheel before the trip.
examples.hard: It took the mechanic three hours to fix the engine, but the car has run perfectly ever since.

examples.easy: What is the price of this?
examples.normal: I'm only buying it if it's the right price.
examples.hard: Food prices have risen sharply this year, so many families are trying to spend less on eating out.

examples.normal: Employers have an obligation to treat all employees equally.
examples.hard: You are under no obligation to buy anything, but the shop will let you try the products for free.

examples.normal: She studied medicine for six years before becoming a doctor.
examples.hard: Modern medicine has made huge progress, and many diseases that once killed millions can now be cured.

examples.easy: We parked in an underground car park.
examples.normal: There is an underground station right next to my office.
examples.hard: The city is planning to build an underground railway to reduce traffic on its busy streets.

examples.normal: The school was originally very small, with only fifty pupils.
examples.hard: The building was originally designed as a hospital, but it was later turned into a hotel.

examples.normal: She is studying chemistry at university in Tashkent.
examples.hard: His interest in chemistry began at school, when a teacher showed the class how to make crystals.

units.name: Lesson 38 - Character, faith and daily life

examples.easy: She has a lot of flowers.
examples.normal: There are a lot of flowers in her garden this spring.
examples.hard: We spent a lot of time looking for a flat, but in the end we found one near my office.

examples.normal: Zip your coat up, because it's cold outside.
examples.hard: I couldn't zip my suitcase because I had packed far too many clothes for a short trip.

examples.normal: Her husband has always been really loyal to her.
examples.hard: The company rewards loyal customers with discounts, which is why many people have shopped there for years.

examples.normal: He was late to the class on purpose because he doesn't like history.
examples.hard: I'm sure she didn't break the vase on purpose; she just wasn't looking where she was going.

examples.normal: No one in our family is more zealous than my father.
examples.hard: The new manager was so zealous about saving money that he even turned off the office heating in winter.

examples.normal: She is the wittiest student in our class and always makes us laugh.
examples.hard: His witty comments made the long meeting much more pleasant, even though nobody agreed on anything.

examples.normal: Many religions teach that everyone will be judged on Judgement Day.
examples.hard: He tried to live an honest life, believing that every person will answer for their actions on Judgement Day.

examples.normal: Every Muslim child learns stories about the Prophet's life.
examples.hard: The teachings of the prophets have shaped the values of millions of people for many centuries.

examples.normal: He found his mother's old handkerchief and started to cry.
examples.hard: My grandfather always kept a clean, folded handkerchief in his jacket pocket, even on hot summer days.

examples.normal: My teacher always makes ablution before he goes to the mosque.
examples.hard: Most mosques have a special room with taps where people can perform ablution before the prayer begins.

examples.normal: She shook hands with her opponent before the match started.
examples.hard: The boxer studied videos of his opponent for weeks so that he would know exactly how he fought.

examples.normal: She looked absolutely stunning in her red wedding dress.
examples.hard: From the top of the mountain we had a stunning view of the lake and the villages in the valley below.

examples.normal: Children love to get money as a gift during Eid.
examples.hard: During Eid, families cook special meals, wear new clothes and visit relatives and neighbours.

examples.normal: Robert is not very good at parking in small spaces.
examples.hard: Parking in the city centre is so expensive that many people now prefer to come in by bus.

examples.easy: There is no telling who will win.
examples.normal: Andijan is losing the match, but there is no telling yet.
examples.hard: There is no telling how long the repairs will take, so we may have to stay in a hotel for a while.

examples.normal: My uncle is a chef, so he is good at hashing meat.
examples.hard: For this dish you need to hash the potatoes and onions before frying them together in a hot pan.

examples.easy: Sop up the water with a cloth.
examples.normal: She used some bread to sop up the sauce on her plate.
examples.hard: After the pipe burst, we spent the whole evening sopping up water from the kitchen floor with old towels.

examples.easy: My mother has a mild voice.
examples.normal: He is a mild man who never raises his voice at anyone.
examples.hard: Despite her mild manner, she was a tough negotiator who always got what she wanted.

examples.normal: These plums are a bit sour, so add some sugar.
examples.hard: The milk had been left out of the fridge all night and had turned sour by the morning.

examples.normal: She had been ill for a week and she looked awful.
examples.hard: The food at the hotel was awful, but the staff were so friendly that we didn't really mind.

examples.normal: Colds are very common in winter, especially among children.
examples.hard: It is quite common for young people in big cities to share a flat with friends to save money.

examples.normal: She was very hardworking and reliable, so they promoted her.
examples.hard: Our hardworking farmers get up before sunrise and often work in the fields until it is dark.

examples.normal: I want an honest answer: do you like my new haircut?
examples.hard: To be honest, I didn't enjoy the film, although the actors did their best with a weak story.

examples.normal: There should be better discipline in schools these days.
examples.hard: Learning a language on your own takes a lot of discipline, because nobody checks that you practise every day.

examples.normal: Most households now own at least one car.
examples.hard: The survey found that the average household spends almost a third of its income on food.

examples.normal: She sat patiently in the waiting room until the doctor called her.
examples.hard: The teacher listened patiently while the nervous student tried to explain why his homework was late again.

examples.normal: They went on a long train journey across India.
examples.hard: The journey from Tashkent to Khiva takes many hours, but the views of the desert make it worthwhile.

examples.easy: Can I have the bill, please?
examples.normal: She always pays her bills on time, so she never has any debts.
examples.hard: Our electricity bill was much higher this winter because we used the heater almost every day.

examples.normal: They made a comparison of different countries' eating habits.
examples.hard: In comparison with last year, sales have increased by twenty per cent, which is excellent news for the company.

examples.normal: It is interesting to compare their situation with ours.
examples.hard: Before you buy a new phone, it's a good idea to compare prices in several shops and online.

examples.normal: They stayed together for the sake of the children.
examples.hard: She gave up smoking for the sake of her health, and now she feels much better than before.

examples.normal: The children got really messy playing in the woods.
examples.hard: Painting with small children is great fun, but it can get very messy, so cover the table first.

examples.normal: He was summoned to appear before the magistrates on Monday.
examples.hard: The witness was summoned to court to give evidence about what she had seen on the night of the robbery.

examples.normal: They decided to proceed with the project despite the cost.
examples.hard: After a short break for questions, the speaker proceeded to explain the second part of the plan.

examples.normal: We had walked further than I had realised.
examples.hard: The hotel was further from the beach than the website suggested, so we had to take a taxi every day.

examples.easy: The baby needs a lot of care.
examples.normal: The standard of care at our local hospital is excellent.
examples.hard: Elderly people who live alone often need extra care, especially during the cold winter months.

examples.normal: He became a doctor after many years of hard study.
examples.hard: What started as a small family business has become one of the biggest companies in the country.

examples.easy: The train is at platform two.
examples.normal: The train to Samarkand leaves from platform three.
examples.hard: We ran along the platform with our heavy bags and jumped on the train just before the doors closed.

examples.easy: I looked everywhere for my keys.
examples.normal: There were people everywhere in the square during the festival.
examples.hard: Mobile phones are everywhere these days, and it's hard to find anyone who doesn't have one.

examples.normal: The male birds are more colourful than the females.
examples.hard: The bazaar was full of colourful fruit, spices and silk scarves that attracted tourists from all over the world.

examples.normal: The speaker underscored the most important points of the plan.
examples.hard: The recent floods underscore the need for better drainage systems in the city's older neighbourhoods.

examples.normal: You can send for a free colour brochure today.
examples.hard: The travel agent gave us a brochure with photos and prices of all the hotels on the coast.

examples.normal: Mix all the ingredients in a bowl and bake for thirty minutes.
examples.hard: The secret of a good plov is fresh ingredients, especially high-quality rice and tender meat.

examples.normal: As I mentioned earlier, there have been a lot of changes recently.
examples.hard: He didn't mention that he was leaving the company until the very last day, which surprised everyone.

examples.normal: 'Some', 'many', 'a lot of' and 'a few' are examples of quantifiers.
examples.hard: Learners often confuse quantifiers like 'much' and 'many', because the choice depends on whether the noun is countable.

examples.normal: The next morning we surveyed the damage caused by the fire.
examples.hard: From the top of the hill, the general surveyed the valley to decide where to place his soldiers.

examples.normal: His average speed on the motorway was 50 miles per hour.
examples.hard: The average salary in the capital is higher than in the regions, but so is the cost of living.

examples.normal: The two sides signed a peace accord last July.
examples.hard: The international accord on climate change was signed by almost every country, but not all of them kept their promises.

examples.normal: Perhaps we could meet for coffee after work tomorrow.
examples.hard: Perhaps the most surprising thing about the city is how quiet it becomes once the tourists have gone home.

examples.normal: Put the fish in the microwave and it will only take five minutes.
examples.hard: Many office workers bring food from home and warm it up in the microwave at lunchtime.

examples.normal: We picked some mushrooms in the forest near our village.
examples.hard: Unfortunately, some poisonous mushrooms look just like edible ones, so never pick them without an expert.

examples.normal: He was one of the best policemen in the whole city.
examples.hard: A policeman stopped the traffic so that the children could cross the busy road safely after school.

examples.normal: She sat in the corner of the room reading a book.
examples.hard: There's a small bakery on the corner of our street that sells the best bread in the neighbourhood.

examples.easy: The bank is opposite the park.
examples.normal: The answers are given on the opposite page.
examples.hard: They live in the house opposite ours, so we see each other almost every morning on the way to work.

examples.normal: She moves with the natural grace of a ballerina.
examples.hard: Even when she lost the final, she accepted defeat with grace and congratulated her opponent warmly.

examples.normal: We expect to see further improvement in the road system next year.
examples.hard: The doctor was pleased to see a clear improvement in her health after only two weeks of treatment.

examples.normal: The weather forecast is for a dry, sunny day tomorrow.
examples.hard: Economists have changed their forecast for next year because prices are rising faster than expected.

examples.normal: Come off the motorway at junction 6.
examples.hard: There was an accident at the busy junction near the station, and traffic was stopped for an hour.

examples.normal: Most problems can be solved by discussion.
examples.hard: After a long discussion, the committee finally agreed to build a new playground in the park.
